newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels say capture key town of Kananga.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels say capture key town of Kananga.

text.p: Zaire rebels said on Monday they had captured the town of Kananga, capital of Western Kasai province and one of the largest towns outside Kinshasa that had still been held by the government.
Kananga fell to rebel forces on Saturday, said Voice of the People radio broadcast from the eastern town of Goma, rebel headquarters.
"The fall of Kananga leaves the Alliance in a good position to move on Bandundu, whose people are eagerly awaiting liberation," the radio said.
There was little looting at the town, close to the Angolan border, because of the vigilance of inhabitants who welcomed rebels, the radio said. There was no independent confirmation.

Zaire government troops, former Rwandan government soldiers and extremist Interahamwe militiamen fled 125 km (78 miles) west to Kananga after their defeat at the diamond capital Mbuji-Mayi, which fell to rebels on April 5, witnesses said.

Rebels of Laurent Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (ADFL) said on Sunday they were resuming their offensive after a three-day halt called to give ailing president Mobutu Sese Seko time to resign.
